title: An antibody-based approach for the _in situ_ evaluation of mouse contribution in human stem cell-derived xenografts
protocol: Deparaffinize tissue sections.
Rehydrate tissue sections.
Section tissues at 2-5 μm thickness.
Mount sections onto positively charged slides.
Dry slides overnight at room temperature in an upright position.
Store prepared slides in a slide box at ambient temperature.
Process stored slides within 3-5 days for optimal staining quality.
Preheat a Coplin staining jar in an incubator at 60°C for ~30 min without the lid.
Load the preheated jar with slides positioned upright.
Incubate slides in the jar for another 30 min at 60°C to melt paraffin wax.
Bake slides to soften paraffin wax.
Incubate sections in xylene for 10 minutes.
Repeat xylene incubation for an additional 10 minutes.
Transfer slides into a staining jar with 2-propanol using forceps.
Incubate the slides in 2-propanol for 5 min.
Wipe off xylene carefully to minimize carryover.
Mix propanol and anhydrous ethanol for tissue de- and rehydration.
Use propanol as the intermediate step to clear most of the xylene.
Proceed through 100% ethanol for ultimate removal of xylene.
Transfer sections through a series of graded ethanol solutions: once through 100%, 70%, and 50% ethanol, 2 minutes each.
Always use absolute grade ethanol (low water content ≤1%) for efficient xylene removal.
Rinse sections three times in distilled H₂O, 5 minutes each.
Keep slides in distilled H₂O until ready to perform antigen retrieval.
Do not allow sections to dry out at any time during the subsequent procedure.
Perform heat-induced epitope retrieval using a microwave oven.
Prepare 1X antigen retrieval buffer and pre-warm in an incubator at 60°C for 10-15 minutes before proceeding.
Transfer approximately 40 ml of pre-heated 1X antigen retrieval buffer into a microwaveable staining jar.
Save the remaining buffer.
Place slides removed from water directly into the retrieval buffer.
Ensure that slides are covered by at least one centimeter of buffer and fully immersed, including half of the slide grip.
Do not screw on the jar cap.
Center the jar inside the microwave.
Adjust the power level to "low", which corresponds to 10% of total power or approximately 80 W.
Turn on the oven and wait until the solution comes to an initial boil, typically 3-6 min.
Boil for 3-5 sec and immediately turn off.
Pause for 10 sec with the door open.
Microwave with the rotation dish on to balance hot and cold spots during heating.
Switch to the "defrost" level for non-continuous heating at 25% power (200 W) and 90-110°C.
Turn on and wait until boiling is initiated, typically <30 sec.
Boil for 1-2 sec and immediately turn off.
Pause for 10 sec with the door open.
Monitor the buffer level in the jar to prevent excessive evaporation or boilover during heating.
Fill up with retrieval buffer if necessary.
Do not allow the slides to dry out at any time during microwaving.
Repeat on/off cycles (step 13) for ~2-4 times.
Follow the antigen retrieval protocol as outlined.
Boil samples according to the specified conditions.
Allow slides to cool to room temperature on benchtop for ~30 min after boiling.
Rinse slides three times in 1X DPBS, 5 min each.
Proceed to immunostaining.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Prepare an appropriate amount of blocking solution for subsequent steps, typically in the range of 200-400 μl per tissue section.
Humidify the moisture chamber by adding dH₂O to the bottom of each slide compartment (approximately 6-7 ml).
Remove slides from 1X DPBS and quickly drain on a paper towel to remove most of the excess liquid.
Do not allow slides to dry completely.
Draw a narrow circle around the tissue section using a liquid-repellent slide marker.
Wait for 5-10 seconds after drawing the circle.
Shake the liquid-repellent slide marker well before each use.
Ensure slides are not allowed to dry out during the staining procedure.
Transfer slides to the moisture chamber after shaking off residual 1X DPBS.
Carefully pipette off excessive amounts of 1X DPBS from the sections without touching the tissue.
Apply ~100-200 μl blocking solution to the sections dropwise.
Ensure the liquid covers the entire area encircled by the hydrophobic barrier, forming a dome-shaped heap within the markings.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Prepare primary antibody and isotype control while incubating.
Dilute Cyclophilin A rabbit monoclonal antibody in blocking solution to a final concentration of 1.3 μg/ml.
Mix gently by inverting and spin down briefly.
Keep the diluted antibody at 4°C until ready to proceed.
Do not switch between different types of blocking solutions during incubation steps.
Use the specified working concentration based on antibody titration for optimal results.
For lot #1 of Cyclophilin A antibody, dilute according to a ratio of 1-2 μl antibody per 100-200 μl blocking solution per tissue section.
Pre-dilute rabbit DA1E monoclonal IgG isotype control 1:20 in 1X DPBS to a concentration of 125 μg/ml.
Further dilute the pre-diluted rabbit IgG in blocking solution to a final concentration of 1.3 μg/ml.
Mix gently by inverting and spin down briefly.
Store pre-diluted IgG aliquoted into working volumes at -20°C for further use.
Thaw only once, with the remainder kept at 4°C for up to 1-2 weeks.
Ensure that the primary antibody and the respective isotype control are concentration-matched.
Pre-dilute the control IgG to avoid pipetting errors.
Prepare cyclophilin A antibody as described above.
Add SMA (1A4) mouse monoclonal antibody to a final concentration of 10 μg/ml.
Mix gently by inverting and spin down briefly.
Keep the mixture at 4°C until ready to proceed.
Prepare rabbit isotype control as described above.
Add mouse MOPC-173 monoclonal IgG₂a isotype control to a final concentration of 10 μg/ml in the blocking solution.
Mix gently by inverting and spin down briefly.
Keep at 4°C until ready to proceed.
Remove slides from the moisture chamber and quickly tilt long edge down to drain off the blocking buffer.
Blot off liquid next to the hydrophobic barrier with a small piece of paper towel without allowing slides to dry completely.
Draw a second hydrophobic barrier right next to the first one before applying antibody solutions.
Apply 100-200 μl diluted primary antibody or isotype control to the sections.
Place the moisture chamber in a fridge or cold room.
Incubate overnight (~16 h) at 4°C.
Prepare a sufficient amount of blocking solution (option A or B) (~100-200 μl/tissue section).
Stick to the same option used the day before.
Remove slides from the moisture chamber and drain off the antibody solution on a paper towel.
Tilt slides against their long edge if mounted with two sections incubated with different antibodies or control reagents.
Transfer slides into a staining jar with 1X DPBS and wash three times for 5 min each.
While washing, prepare fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody.
Dilute Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG 1:500 in blocking solution (option A or B) to a final concentration of 4 μg/ml.
Mix gently by inverting and spin down briefly.
Protect the diluted antibody from light until ready to proceed.
Prepare Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG as described above.
Add Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG at a dilution of 1:500 to yield a final concentration of 4 μg/ml.
Mix gently by inverting.
Spin down briefly.
Remove slides from 1X DPBS and shake off excess liquid.
Place slides in the moisture chamber.
Add 100-200 μl diluted fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody onto the sections.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Remove slides from the moisture chamber and drain off the antibody solution on a paper towel.
Transfer slides into a staining jar with 1X DPBS and wash three times, 5 min each.
While washing, prepare an appropriate amount (~30-40 ml) of DAPI working solution and transfer into a staining jar.
Remove slides from 1X DPBS and quickly drain on a paper towel.
Counterstain sections by immersing slides for 3-5 min in the DAPI solution.
Carefully drain off the DAPI solution and rinse slides once in 1X DPBS for 5 min.
Keep slides in 1X DPBS until ready to perform coverslipping.
Apply ~4-8 20 μl-drops of antifade mounting medium directly to a coverslip.
Remove slides from 1X DPBS.
Quickly drain slides on a paper towel.
Vigorously shake off residual liquid.
Lay slides section side down over the coverslip.
Absorb excess mounting medium with a paper towel.
Store mounted slides flat or on the edge at 4°C protected from light.
Subject slides to microscopic evaluation.
Run a pilot experiment with a limited number of samples to establish an appropriate imaging protocol.
Set parameters such as excitation intensity, detector gain, and exposure time for optimal results.
Incorporate transmitted light imaging mode (e.g., phase contrast) if available.
Acquire phase contrast and confocal epifluorescence images simultaneously.
Merge the images to determine the precise location of labeled cells within the tissue.
Use the same imaging and post-acquisition protocols for all samples, positive controls, and negative controls.
